StackType.issue: PowerStackType.Single, and the sim overrides Power.on_stack to `pass` citing it -- which is WRONG about C# and inert about this power. Single means only 'Amount is hidden, and is always 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13); PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 adds the offset with no StackType branch at all, so in the game a second application really does raise Amount to 2. This unit is one of the 15 the stack census flags (py audit/tools/power_census.py stack) and the main report's section 7 item 5 covers the class. DORMANT here for the per-unit reason the census leaves open: nothing reads this power's Amount -- not the power itself, not any sim listener, and not the C# model (whose only Amount reader is the hidden DisplayAmount). Named trigger: any future effect that scales with the stack count, or a UI that shows it. The one ported applier applies exactly 1 (cards/colorless_skills.py:770-772) and the power kills its owner the first time it fires, so a second stack is doubly unobservable.

AfterDamageReceived.issue: The hook is the RIGHT one this time -- C# really is AfterDamageReceived, not a before-hook, so this unit does NOT have power/thorns's and power/curl_up's defect -- and the guards line up: target == base.Owner, props.IsPoweredAttack() and result.UnblockedDamage > 0 (TheGambitPower.cs:18) vs target is self.owner, is_powered_attack(props) and amount > 0 (powers.py:3826), where the sim's `amount` argument is hp_lost, i.e. post-block (cmds.py:122 passes the value written at :90-92). The GAP is the killing-blow interaction, PROMPT.md bug class 2. cmds.py:121 guards the whole dispatch with `if not target.is_dead`, mirroring CreatureCmd.cs:392, so when the hit that got through ALSO reduced the owner to 0 HP the sim never fires this hook -- and C# does not fire it either, for the same reason. So far so equal. Where they diverge is DEATH PREVENTION: cmds.py:96-113 runs should_die and, when a listener prevents the death, floors the owner at 1 HP and clears is_dead, after which cmds.py:121 lets this hook fire and it kills the owner outright via CreatureCmd.kill (powers.py:3829) -- bypassing the prevention the engine just honoured. In C# the same sequence runs but CreatureCmd.Kill is itself subject to the death pipeline, so the preventer gets a second say. DORMANT: the sim's should_die preventers are the Illusion revive (an enemy-only power) and Fairy in a Bottle, and The Gambit is player-only, so the pair is not currently co-reachable. Named trigger: porting any player-side death preventer, or applying The Gambit to an Illusion.

guards.rationale: powers.py:3828 _expires before CreatureCmd.kill at :3829 -- the same order, and the order matters: removing first is what stops the kill's own damage path from re-entering this hook. The sim's _expire (powers.py:86-92) pops the power and unregisters it; C#'s PowerCmd.Remove (PowerCmd.cs:287-295) additionally fires power.AfterRemoved, which this power does not implement. Observationally identical, same treatment as the _expire entries in audits/power/duplication.json and audits/power/flame_barrier.json per binding rule 3.
cmds.py's CreatureCmd.kill. Same verb; the divergence in what the death pipeline then does is carried by the hook entry above rather than duplicated here.

powers.py:3826 is_powered_attack(props) (valueprops.py). Present and correct -- so unblocked POISON or Constrict damage does not trigger it on either side. Contrast power/thorns, whose port dropped exactly this gate.

The sim's on_damage_received amount is hp_lost, computed after block absorption and after modify_hp_lost (cmds.py:86-92), so `amount <= 0 -> return` (powers.py:3826) is the same test. A fully blocked attack does not kill the owner on either side.
